item.title: Hug a user is here! Tell us what’s broken, we’ll fix it
item.description:
We’re starting something new at daily.dev called Hug a User.


The idea is simple: Every week, each engineer gets up to half a day to fix a bug or ship a small feature that came directly from you. No tickets. No sprints. No begging for approvals (unless it’s the homepage, then yes, still sacred ground).



Basically, it’s your chance to have an engineer swoop in, cape and all, and make that one annoying thing disappear.


What counts?



  • Fixing a bug that’s been haunting you

  • Polishing rough edges that slow you down

  • Small features that would make your daily.dev experience smoother


What doesn’t count?



  • Asking us to build GitHub 2.0 in half a day

  • Secret plots to sneak your pet feature onto the homepage


So, tell us what’s the one bug, frustration, or small improvement you’d love to see us tackle in Hug a User?


Drop it in the comments, and who knows, next week you might log in and it’ll just be fixed.


(And yes, if you’ve ever cursed at daily.dev under your breath, now’s the time to turn that energy into a feature request.)
item.author: Nimrod Kramer

item.title: Announcing Spin 3.4
item.description: Spin 3.4 introduces HTTP/2 support for outgoing requests, enabling seamless integration with gRPC-based backends and improving performance through multiplexed connections. The release adds PostgreSQL connection pooling for better database performance and expands supported data types including UUID, JSONB, and array types. Additionally, Spin templates now include schema directives in spin.toml files for automatic validation and code completion in editors.

item.title: The end of notification hell
item.description:
Let’s be real - our old notification settings were… kinda lame. Patches on patches, broad toggles, zero finesse. We (finally) fixed that because our goal was simple: turn notifications into something actually useful, not just noise.


This is a complete makeover:



  • Ultimate control - Choose exactly what you get and where you get it: in-app, push, or email.

  • Granular as hell - Comments on your posts? Replies to your replies? Upvotes, mentions, Awards, cores, report updates? You decide!

  • Follow smarter - Fine-tune notifications for sources, users, collections, read later, streaks, achievements.

  • Creators rejoice - A whole section just for creator alerts so you never miss the metrics that matter.

  • Squads, finally fixed - One place for all your Squad notifications. And if you’re an admin or a mod, you now get pinpoint control for new members, posts awaiting review, milestones, and more.


Best part? You can split every single preference across in-app, push, and email. And you’ll find it all centralized in one screen. No hunting around. No more one-size-fits-none.


Building this wasn’t as simple as adding a few new toggles. Notifications touch almost every part of daily.dev - posts, comments, Squads, creators, achievements, moderation, email, push, in-app.


Untangling years of patch-on-patch logic and rebuilding it into one unified system was a massive refactor. It meant rethinking data flows, syncing across multiple channels, and making sure every edge case was covered so you don’t get spammed (or miss something important). It’s one of those projects that sounds small on the surface but is surprisingly hard to get right… which is exactly why we’re proud to finally ship it.


👉 Go and play with it yourself: app.daily.dev/settings/notifications


From now on, notifications aren’t spam. They’re a signal. And the signal is yours to control.

item.title: DeepSeek-V3.1 Release: A New Era in Open AI Technology
item.description:
Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has unveiled its latest innovation, the V3.1 large language model, revolutionizing the landscape of open AI with its groundbreaking capabilities. This model, with a staggering 685-billion parameters, competes head-to-head with proprietary systems from major industry players like OpenAI and Anthropic but with a significant cost advantage. Notably, V3.1 achieves an impressive 71.6% on coding benchmarks, signaling its robust performance in real-world applications.


One of the distinguishing features of DeepSeek V3.1 is its hybrid architecture, seamlessly integrating chat, reasoning, and coding functionalities within a unified framework. This architectural evolution is augmented by its hybrid inference capabilities, introducing “Think” and “Non-Think” modes. These modes offer users enhanced reasoning speed and improved agent functionalities, pushing the boundaries of traditional AI capabilities.


The release includes substantial updates, such as support for a 128,000 token context, ensuring comprehensive and extended text processing. The updated model is compatible with the Anthropic API format, includes strict function calling in beta, and provides API updates that cater to various practical applications.


From a technical perspective, V3.1 demonstrates optimized performance for new Chinese chips, utilizing the UE8M0 FP8 data type. This progression hints at the potential of forthcoming domestic silicon from Chinese tech giants like Huawei, given the current limitations of chips like the Ascend 910C in supporting FP8 natively.


Available for free on platforms like Hugging Face, the model challenges conventional AI business strategies by delivering frontier-level capabilities without imposing usage restrictions or licensing fees. Alongside the open-source availability of weights, the model sets a new benchmark in accessible AI technology.


The revised pricing model for the API will be effective from September 5th, 2025, but the focus remains on affordability and expansive access. DeepSeek V3.1 represents a significant leap in AI technology, effectively democratizing access to cutting-edge advancements and heralding a new era of AI accessibility and capability.

item.title: Next.js 15.5
item.description: Next.js 15.5 introduces Turbopack builds in beta with significant performance improvements (2-5x faster builds), stable Node.js middleware runtime support, enhanced TypeScript features including typed routes and automatic route props helpers, deprecation of the next lint command in favor of direct ESLint usage, and deprecation warnings for features being removed in Next.js 16 including AMP support and legacyBehavior for links.

item.title: google/mangle
item.description: Mangle is Google's open-source programming language that extends Datalog for deductive database programming. It enables querying data from multiple sources uniformly and supports recursive rules, aggregation, and function calls. The language is particularly useful for vulnerability detection, dependency analysis, and knowledge graph modeling. Implemented as a Go library, Mangle can be embedded into applications and offers practical extensions beyond traditional Datalog while maintaining accessibility for developers.

item.title: Keep a Developer Log (Your Future Self Will Thank You)
item.description: A developer shares their experience with maintaining a daily development log, explaining how this simple practice has improved their workflow, memory management, and team communication. The log template includes tasks, technical debt tracking, team notes, meeting summaries, and detailed work breakdowns. Benefits include freeing up mental space, better preparation for meetings, increased visibility of technical debt, systematic problem-solving approach, and the ability to track personal growth over time. The practice requires only 5-10 minutes daily but provides significant long-term value for context retention and team collaboration.
